cards.name: Pop-art colour halftone
cards.summary: A photo or illustration is rebuilt from big overlapping cyan, magenta, yellow and black dots on rotated screens, the enlarged-print rosette of pop art.
use_for: bold social backgrounds from a plain photo
avoid: small output sizes with a large radius: the image dissolves into dots; scale the radius to the print size
faces you need to recognise at a glance: keep the original underneath at partial opacity
files going to a real CMYK press: the simulated dots clash with the press screen (moire); flatten to a high resolution and proof

steps.note: Duplicate the photo layer so the original stays untouched (or convert it to a smart object for a smart filter).
Optional punch first: Image > Adjustments > Brightness/Contrast (verified: brighter, ends held near black and white).

Filter > Pixelate > Color Halftone: radius 12 px with the classic screen angles (verified frame: overlapping CMY-style dots with a rosette, pure saturated colours). Radius 20+ for a poster seen from far away.

On the placed image or the artwork group: Effect > Pixelate > Color Halftone, same angles. Illustrator runs Photoshop Effects as raster effects at Document Raster Effects Settings resolution: set 300 ppi for print first.
Convert to Bitmap first if the artwork is vector (the effect works on bitmaps).
Effects > Color Transform > Halftone at the largest dot (verified: coarse CMYK screen with rosettes). The Black angle key was dropped in the test, so leave it at its default.

cards.name: Newsprint mono halftone
cards.summary: A photo printed like an old newspaper: one black dot screen whose dots grow with the shadows, on a warm off-white paper tone with a little ink speckle.
use_for: background photos that must stay quiet behind type
avoid: fine detail you need to read: a coarse screen erases it
shrinking the result afterwards: resampled dots turn to grey mush or moire; build it at final size
the Photoshop Bitmap route on an RGB document: Image > Mode > Bitmap only works on Grayscale

steps.note: Image > Mode > Grayscale on a copy of the document (verified: colour channels become one Gray channel).
Image > Mode > Bitmap: changeMode(ChangeMode.BITMAP, options) with a BitmapConversionOptions (next step); flattens the layers.
method = HALFTONESCREEN, resolution = output ppi (e.g. 300), frequency = 20-35 lines per inch for a visible dot, angle = 45, shape = ROUND.
Back to Grayscale (then RGB) so the paper tone can be added on a layer above in Multiply.

steps.name: Add Noise
steps.note: Faint monochrome speckle like ink and paper fibre (verified: Add Noise at 25 % is strong; keep it low).

On the placed photo: Effect > Sketch > Halftone Pattern, Dot type, small size, low contrast; the sketch effects use the default black and white. Illustrator runs Photoshop Effects as raster effects at Document Raster Effects Settings resolution: set 300 ppi for print first.
Image in Multiply over a rectangle in the paper colour (#EFE8D8) so the white turns into paper.
Bitmaps > Mode > Grayscale (8-bit).
Bitmaps > Mode > Black and White (1-bit) with the Halftone conversion method, round dots, 20-35 lpi (dialog; the object-model route ConvertToBW is unverified).
Optional, on a grayscale copy before the 1-bit step: light Gaussian intensity noise for ink grit.

manual_steps: CorelDRAW: the 1-bit halftone conversion settings live in the Black and White dialog.
A 1-bit bitmap in CorelDRAW or Illustrator can then be coloured: its black pixels take the object's fill colour.

cards.name: Risograph two-ink print
cards.summary: Two flat fluorescent inks (typically pink and blue) printed as grainy halftones that overlap into a third colour and sit slightly out of register.
use_for: indie posters, zines and event flyers
a warm, imperfect alternative to full colour
avoid: brand colours that must match exactly: riso inks and offsets are approximate by design
more than two or three inks: the look turns muddy
large solid areas of both inks: they overprint dark; give each ink its own parts of the image

steps.note: Duplicate the (greyscale-looking) image layer: the bottom copy becomes ink 1, the top copy ink 2. Desaturate both first.

steps.name: Desaturate
steps.note: Image > Adjustments > Desaturate on each copy (verified: flat greyscale).
Ink 1 (bottom copy): Filter > Sketch > Halftone Pattern, Dot (scratchDisks): a black-and-white dot screen (verified frame). Use the default black / white colours.
Ink 2 (top copy): Stamp gives flat two-tone shapes for the second ink (verified: smoothed black / white like a rubber stamp).

steps.name: Color Overlay
steps.note: On ink 1: Screen with fluorescent pink turns black to pink and keeps white white. On ink 2 the same with riso blue #0078BF.
Both ink layers in Multiply so white drops out and the overlap prints as a dark purple (the render matched the Multiply formula; 'wrong' refers to an outdated plate sentence).
translate(3, 2) on ink 2: the deliberate misregistration.

steps.name: Grain
steps.note: On a merged copy: stippled grain for the drum texture (verified: Grain is strong; keep intensity low). Untested: stippled was not the rendered type (enlarged was).
Edit Colors > Recolor with Preset > Two Color on the artwork, mapping it onto the two ink colours (menu path only: no executeMenuCommand id is known).
Put each ink's objects on its own layer and set them to Multiply so overlaps darken like ink.
On the second ink's group: move 1.5 pt right and 1 pt down, no copies: the misregistration (vertical sign unconfirmed).
Effect > Texture > Grain on each ink group for the print texture. Illustrator runs Photoshop Effects as raster effects at Document Raster Effects Settings resolution: set 300 ppi for print first.
Grayscale (8-bit) on the bitmap.
Bitmaps > Mode > Duotone (8-bit): two inks, pink and blue, each with its own curve (dialog; misregistration is not possible inside one duotone).
Ink grit: spike noise at low density (verified Add Noise; spike was not the rendered mode). Apply before the duotone step if the dialog refuses noise on a duotone bitmap.

manual_steps: CorelDRAW: pick the two inks and shape their curves in the Duotone dialog.
Illustrator: decide which objects print in which ink (the Two Color recolour mapping) by eye.

cards.name: Screen-print flat colour
cards.summary: An image reduced to a handful of flat ink colours with simplified, slightly rough shapes, like a hand-pulled screen print or gig poster.
use_for: T-shirt and merch artwork (limited ink count)
avoid: subtle gradients and skin tones you need to keep: they band into flat steps
type inside the image: the simplification breaks small letters into shards; set type on top afterwards
real screen-print separations from the Photoshop result alone: trace to vector so each ink is a clean shape

steps.note: Posterize adjustment layer above the image: 4 levels per channel snaps tones into flat bands (verified screen-print look).
On the image layer: Filter > Artistic > Cutout rebuilds it from flat colour levels with roughly cut edges (verified; it breaks type into shards, as warned).

steps.name: Add Noise
steps.note: A trace of ink texture.

On the placed photo: Image Trace with a 4-6 colour preset and expand it into flat filled shapes (object model: placedItem.trace(), then tracing.expandTracing(); set the colour count in the Image Trace panel).
A very small corner roughen on the traced group makes the edges look cut by hand (verified: sharp irregular teeth at 12 pt; here 1.5 pt).
Effects > Color Transform > Posterize: 4 levels (verified).
Outline Trace > Clipart (PowerTRACE) to turn the posterised bitmap into flat filled shapes; set the colour count in the dialog.

manual_steps: Illustrator and CorelDRAW: the trace colour count and smoothing are set in the Image Trace panel / PowerTRACE dialog.

cards.name: Comic book ink and dots
cards.summary: A photo turned into comic art: flat posterised colour, dark ink lines along the contrast edges and a dot screen showing in the shadows.
avoid: low-contrast or soft photos: the edge lines come out patchy; add contrast first
serious or sensitive news photos: the cartoon look trivialises them

steps.note: Duplicate the photo layer.
Bottom copy: Filter > Artistic > Poster Edges: flat posterised tones with dark lines along the edges (verified printed-poster look).
Top copy: Color Halftone at a small radius for the dot screen.
Top copy in Multiply at 30-50 % opacity so the dots show mainly in the shadows (formula-verified mode).
On the placed photo: Effect > Artistic > Poster Edges. Illustrator runs Photoshop Effects as raster effects at Document Raster Effects Settings resolution: set 300 ppi for print first.
On a copy in front (Paste in Front), set to Multiply at 40 %: Color Halftone dots.
The dotted copy in Multiply.
Posterize to 4 levels for flat colour.
Halftone at a small dot radius over the posterised image.

manual_steps: CorelDRAW: for ink outlines, trace a Find Edges copy (Effects > Contour > Find Edges, Solid) with Outline Trace > Line Art and lay the black lines on top.

cards.name: Grunge distressed print
cards.summary: Artwork or type looks worn: ragged sprayed edges, speckled ink drop-outs and a rough surface grain, like a weathered poster or a well-used stamp.
avoid: corporate and clean-tech layouts
small text: drop-outs make it unreadable; distress only display sizes
print files that need crisp vector edges: the effect is raster

steps.note: Rasterize the type or shape layer (or work on a flattened copy).
Filter > Brush Strokes > Spatter: edges turn ragged and speckled (verified), fills keep their colour.

steps.name: Grain
steps.note: Speckle grain for ink drop-outs (verified Grain; Speckle was not the rendered type).

steps.name: Texturizer
steps.note: Low sandstone relief for a rough surface (verified Texturizer, brick at 14; keep relief low).
On the type outlines or shapes: small corner roughen for chipped edges.
Effect > Brush Strokes > Spatter: sprayed, ragged edges. Illustrator runs Photoshop Effects as raster effects at Document Raster Effects Settings resolution: set 300 ppi for print first.
Effect > Texture > Grain, speckle, for drop-outs.
Convert to Bitmap (bitmap effects need pixels).
Spike noise for speckle (verified Add Noise; spike not the rendered mode).
Effects > Texture > Stone at medium roughness: a lit pitted surface over the art, colours kept (verified at 100 / 100).

manual_steps: A scanned paper or wall texture over the art in Multiply (your own scan) gives the most convincing grunge; none ships with this recipe.

cards.name: Printed-on-paper texture
cards.summary: Flat digital artwork picks up the feel of uncoated paper or canvas: a fine embossed tooth, a slight warm tone and soft grain.
use_for: illustrations and posters that feel too digital
avoid: UI and screen graphics that must stay crisp
large relief values: the texture overpowers the art
CorelDRAW Wave Paper when colours must hold: its render faded colours strongly toward pastel

steps.note: Filter > Texture > Texturizer, canvas tooth lit from the top left (verified: relief embossed over the frame, colours kept).
Photo Filter adjustment layer: a slight warm paper cast (verified with a cool filter, luminosity kept).

steps.name: Add Noise
steps.note: Fine fibre grain.

Effect > Texture > Texturizer, canvas, light top left, on the artwork group. Illustrator runs Photoshop Effects as raster effects at Document Raster Effects Settings resolution: set 300 ppi for print first.
Cleanest route: a rectangle filled with the paper colour on top, given a bitmap pattern transparency from your own paper scan (FileName = that file; verified with a photo as the pattern).
Alternative on a bitmap: Effects > Art Strokes > Wave Paper lays a grainy paper texture (verified) but fades colours toward pastel.

manual_steps: Supply your own paper scan for the CorelDRAW bitmap-pattern transparency (no texture file ships with PGD).

cards.name: Torn-paper collage piece
cards.summary: A photo or colour block sits on a scrap of paper with a ragged torn edge and a soft shadow, ready to layer into a collage.
avoid: perfectly repeating edges: tear each piece with a new random seed or the collage looks stamped
tiny pieces: a torn edge needs at least 300 px to read

steps.note: On a white or paper-coloured rectangle: corner points, fine detail, a few points of size: a jagged torn edge (verified: sharp irregular teeth).
Soft shadow right and down so the scrap lifts off the page (verified: shadow offset right / down for positive values).
For a photo scrap: a second roughened shape over the photo, both selected, Make Clipping Mask.
Zipper distortion with Random on and Smooth off gives an irregular torn edge (card: Random for torn paper). Untested: the verified frame had Random and Smooth off.
Soft shadow down-right.
Place the photo inside the torn shape (AddToPowerClip). Untested: PowerClip is a needs_input card with no render test.
Layer > Rasterize > Shape on the paper rectangle layer.
Spatter roughens the rectangle's edges into a ragged, fibrous border (verified: edges ragged and speckled).

steps.name: Drop Shadow
steps.note: Soft shadow down-right of the scrap.
Put the photo layer above the scrap and Create Clipping Mask so it shows only inside the torn shape.

manual_steps: CorelDRAW: the Roughen tool brushes a torn edge onto part of an outline by hand (no script call).

cards.name: Woodcut / linocut print
cards.summary: A photo becomes a bold two-tone relief print: solid black ink shapes with carved, slightly rough edges on paper.
avoid: busy, low-contrast photos: the two-tone cut loses the subject; pick a strong silhouette
fine facial detail: it fills in; crop tighter

steps.name: Desaturate
steps.note: Greyscale first.
Filter > Sketch > Stamp: flat smoothed black-and-white shapes like a rubber stamp or lino block (verified). Balance sets how much goes black.
Optional: Torn Edges adds ragged, fibrous borders to the black shapes (verified two-tone with ragged edges).
Lay the result in Multiply over a paper colour layer so white becomes paper.
On the placed photo: Effect > Sketch > Stamp. Illustrator runs Photoshop Effects as raster effects at Document Raster Effects Settings resolution: set 300 ppi for print first.
For true vector cuts: rasterise the stamped result and Image Trace it in black and white, then expand.
Effects > Art Strokes > Scraperboard in White mode: black surface with scratched white strokes, the closest scripted carved-print look (verified in Color mode; White mode not rendered).

cards.name: Line engraving
cards.summary: A photo rendered as fine engraved lines whose thickness follows the tone, the banknote / old-print engraving look.
use_for: editorial illustrations with a classic print feel
avoid: small output: the lines merge into grey; keep the line count low for small sizes
screens with scaling: line screens moire when resized; export at final size

steps.note: Filter > Sketch > Halftone Pattern, Line: horizontal lines that thicken in the shadows (verified as a dot screen; the Line type was not rendered).
Alternative: Graphic Pen draws fine parallel ink strokes, dense in the dark areas (verified, left diagonal).
On the placed photo: Effect > Sketch > Graphic Pen. Illustrator runs Photoshop Effects as raster effects at Document Raster Effects Settings resolution: set 300 ppi for print first.
Effects > Art Strokes > Pen & Ink, Crosshatch: a black crosshatch ink drawing on white (verified).
Alternative: Etching turns it into an engraved metal plate in one surface colour (verified: deep grooves lit from the upper left).
